useCase.name: Cancel a charge billed in error against which no money has been received

intent.name: fee.cancellation.raise
intent.summary: Propose cancelling a charge that should never have been raised and against which no money has been received. One step, and it cancels nothing on its own.
routesHere: raise a cancellation for this invoice — it was billed to the wrong student

routesHere.text: ye bill galat student ke naam bana hai, cancel karwana hai
routesHere.gloss: this bill was raised against the wrong student, it needs cancelling

routesHere.text: duplicate invoice ban gaya hai, cancel karo
routesHere.gloss: a duplicate invoice was created, cancel it

routesHere.text: ye bacha to chhod chuka tha, phir bhi bill ban gaya
routesHere.gloss: this child had already left and was billed anyway

routesHere: propose cancelling the whole batch we raised for the wrong period

request.text: family ne paisa de diya hai, phir bhi charge galat tha
request.gloss: the family has paid but the charge was wrong

routesElsewhere.note: This applies only where no money has been received. A wrong charge already paid is a credit, because the school is holding the family's money (BR-2).

request.text: ye debt wasool nahi hoga, maaf kar do
request.gloss: this debt will not be recovered, write it off

routesElsewhere.note: A write-off recognises a loss on a correctly raised charge. Using it for a billing error is the wrong instrument (UC-04-09 BR-2).
Cancelling raises nothing in its place. The correct charge is raised through the ordinary invoice run (BR-10).

request.text: bill ka aadha hissa cancel karo

routesElsewhere.note: A cancellation is for the whole invoice. Cancelling part is done by cancelling it and raising the correct one in its place (BR-3).

steps.note: One step, and it produces a proposal at Awaiting approval. Nothing is cancelled, nothing posts and the family is told nothing until a School Admin approves it (BR-1).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A payment against the invoice, a missing description, and an invoice already cancelled or written off are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the cancellation proposal with its reason and description, together with the audit entry or not at all. The invoice is untouched and still owed, no ledger entry posts, and nothing is sent to the family. For a batch scope, the paid invoices in it are identified and reported now rather than at approval (E7), so the approver sees what will and will not be cancelled.

operations.name: fee.cancellation.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: invoice_id or batch_id, since one invoice carries one open cancellation at a time
operations.purpose: Raise a cancellation proposal against an unpaid invoice, or a whole batch raised in error, with the reason and a written description.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: One invoice, or a whole batch raised in error (BR-8).

parameters.name: invoice_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No unpaid issued invoice matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, period and amount.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Invoice. Must carry no payment (BR-2, E1).

parameters.name: batch_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with batch number, scope, period and invoice count.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Batch.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Billed to the wrong student | Wrong amount | Wrong billing period | Duplicate of another invoice | Student had left | Structure applied in error | Other
parameters.notes: Why the charge should not have been raised (BR-4). Read from what the actor stated, never chosen to fit.

parameters.name: description
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. What actually went wrong, in terms a reader can follow (BR-4, E2). The actor's own words — an invoice that disappeared with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: cancellation_id
fields.description: The proposal.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Awaiting approval. Nothing is cancelled yet.

fields.name: amount_to_cancel
fields.description: The invoice's outstanding amount. Never typed and never partial (BR-3).

fields.name: invoice_count
fields.description: For a batch scope, how many invoices would be cancelled.

fields.name: paid_invoices
fields.description: For a batch scope, those that have been paid and will be refused (BR-8, E7). Shown now so the approver knows.

fields.name: concession_to_return
fields.description: Concession the invoice consumed, returned on approval (BR-7).

fields.name: credit_to_return
fields.description: Family credit the invoice consumed, returned on approval (BR-7).

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not also approve it (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A payment has been recorded against the invoice.
errors.note: The message names the amount and date. This is a credit, not a cancellation (BR-2) — the school is holding the family's money.

errors.meaning: No reason or description was given.
errors.note: Message: "Describe what went wrong. A cancelled charge has to be explainable." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The invoice has already been cancelled.
The invoice has been written off.
errors.note: A written-off debt is a recognised loss on a correct charge. Cancelling it would say the charge was wrong, which is a different statement.

errors.meaning: Some invoices in the batch have been paid.
errors.written: The proposal covers the unpaid ones.
errors.note: Listed. Those need a credit under UC-04-10, which is a separate decision (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the description. An invoice that disappeared with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first (BR-4), and a description a planner wrote explains what it guessed rather than what went wrong.
Never choose the reason to fit. It is a fixed list read for patterns afterwards; "Other" used as a default makes the list stop meaning anything, and a wrong code hides a recurring billing fault.

Never use a cancellation where money has been received. E1 is BR-2 working — the school is holding the family's money, and cancelling the bill would leave the payment with nothing to sit against. That is a credit under UC-04-10.
Never chain the approval. A cancellation is raised by one person and approved by another, because a charge that can be raised and removed by one hand is not a control (BR-1).
Never chain a corrected invoice onto a cancellation. Cancelling raises nothing in its place; the correct charge goes through the ordinary run as a separate, deliberate act (BR-10).
Report the paid invoices in a batch proposal. They will be refused (BR-8), and the approver needs to know that approving this cancels 18 of 20 rather than all of them.

reversal.statement: A proposal is not withdrawn by anything written here — it is approved or returned by the School Admin. Nothing has been cancelled and no family has been told, so an unwanted proposal simply is not approved. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: ye bill galat student ke naam bana hai — Ayesha ka bill Bilal ke against laga hai

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on an unpaid invoice.

inputs.description: Ayesha's September tuition was billed against Bilal's account in error.

steps.note: The description is the actor's own account of what went wrong (PR-1). The reason is read from what they said, not chosen to fit (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A proposal at Awaiting approval. Bilal's invoice is still owed and still on the overdue list until a School Admin approves it. The correct charge against Ayesha is a separate act afterwards (BR-10).

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on an invoice with PKR 4,000 received.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged; the plan does not test for the payment beforehand. The API returns PAYMENT_RECEIVED (E1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is raised. Report that PKR 4,000 was received on 08-09-2026, so this is a credit rather than a cancellation — the school is holding the family's money and cancelling the bill would leave it sitting against nothing (PR-3).

request.text: poore batch ka bill galat period ka tha, cancel karwao
request.gloss: the whole batch was billed for the wrong period, get it cancelled

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on a batch of 20 where 2 have been paid.

inputs.description: The batch was raised for October against September's period.

resolvedPlans.outcome: A proposal covering the 18 unpaid invoices, with the 2 paid ones listed and excluded (E7). Report both numbers to the approver — approving this cancels 18, not 20, and the other 2 need a credit (PR-6).

intent.name: fee.cancellation.approve
intent.summary: Approve a cancellation, which withdraws the charge, posts the balancing entry and tells the family. School Admin only, one step.
routesHere: approve the cancellation on Bilal's September invoice

routesHere.text: ye charge cancel kar do, proposal aa chuka hai
routesHere.gloss: cancel this charge, the proposal has come through

routesHere: sign off the batch cancellation Accounts raised

routesElsewhere.note: A return needs a reason so Accounts know what to correct.
Accounts raise; School Admin approves. One hand cannot do both (BR-1).
Cancelling raises nothing in its place (BR-10).

steps.note: One step, and it is the act that withdraws the charge. The balancing entry posts, the invoice moves to Cancelled, any concession or family credit it consumed is returned, and the family is told.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the acting user raised the proposal themselves, and whether the ledger posting succeeds, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the balancing ledger entry, the invoice's status, the returned concession and credit, and the audit entry together or not at all (E6). Nothing is deleted and nothing is edited — the original entry stays in place, so the books show both what was billed and what was withdrawn (BR-5, BR-6). Where the original accounting period has closed, the entry posts to the current open one; a closed period is not reopened to tidy a mistake (BR-9). The invoice leaves overdue tracking and stops accruing late fee at once (BR-12). The message to the family is separate and does not block (E8) — but it matters, because a challan already in their hands must not be paid by mistake (BR-11).

operations.name: fee.cancellation.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: cancellation_id, since a proposal carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a cancellation, post the balancing entry, mark the invoice cancelled, return what it consumed and tell the family.

parameters.name: cancellation_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No cancellation proposal matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The cancellation proposal, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was cancelled and what came back.

fields.name: cancellation_id
fields.description: The approved cancellation.

fields.name: invoices_cancelled
fields.description: invoice_number and amount for each.

fields.name: invoices_refused
fields.description: For a batch, those paid and therefore refused (BR-8, E7).

fields.name: amount_cancelled
fields.description: The total withdrawn.

fields.name: concession_returned
fields.description: Returned to the student, so a family does not lose a discount because the school billed them wrongly (BR-7).

fields.name: credit_returned
fields.description: Returned to the family code (BR-7).

fields.name: posted_to_period
fields.description: The current open period where the original's has closed (BR-9).

fields.name: family_notified
fields.description: Delivery status. A challan already in their hands must not be paid by mistake (BR-11).

fields.name: removed_from_overdue
fields.description: The invoice leaves overdue tracking and stops accruing late fee (BR-12).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve their own cancellation.
errors.note: Only a School Admin approves (BR-1). In practice the capability is absent from an Accounts allow-list.
Message: "The cancellation could not be posted. Nothing has changed."

errors.meaning: Some invoices in the batch have been paid.
The message to the family failed.
errors.written: The cancellation, the posting and the status all stand.
errors.notWritten: The family has not been told.
errors.note: Report both halves — a family holding a challan for a withdrawn charge will take it to the bank (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never approve a cancellation the acting user raised. E3 is BR-1 working — a charge that can be raised and removed by one hand is not a control.
Report the concession and credit returned. A family must not lose a discount because the school billed them wrongly (BR-7), and the amounts coming back are the proof that they did not.
Report whether the family was told. A challan already in their hands must not be paid by mistake (BR-11), and a failed message means somebody has to phone them.
Never chain a replacement invoice onto an approval. Cancelling raises nothing in its place (BR-10); the correct charge is a separate, deliberate run.
Report the posting period where it differs. A closed period is not reopened to tidy a mistake (BR-9), so a September cancellation may sit in November's books — which is correct and worth saying.

reversal.statement: A cancellation is not reversed. The original entry and the balancing entry both stay in the books (BR-5), and where the charge is owed after all it is raised afresh through the ordinary invoice run — a new invoice with a new number, not the old one restored. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

intent.name: fee.cancellation.return
intent.summary: Send a cancellation proposal back to Accounts with what is wrong with it. School Admin only, one step.
routesHere: return this cancellation — the description doesn't explain anything

routesHere.text: cancellation wapas bhej do, wajah saaf nahi hai
routesHere.gloss: send the cancellation back, the reason is not clear

routesHere.text: ye cancel nahi hona chahiye, wapas karo
routesHere.gloss: this should not be cancelled, send it back

routesHere: send it back, this looks like it should be a credit

routesElsewhere.note: Returning says so; raising the credit is Accounts' work in their own session.

steps.note: One step. Nothing is cancelled and nothing posts; the proposal goes back to Accounts with the reason.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The reason is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the status change, the reason and the audit entry together or not at all. The invoice is untouched, still owed and still on the overdue list. Nothing is sent to the family.

operations.name: fee.cancellation.return
operations.purpose: Send a cancellation proposal back to Accounts with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: cancellation_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No cancellation proposal matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The cancellation proposal, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required — Accounts have to know what to correct. The School Admin's own words.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: cancellation_id
fields.description: The proposal.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Returned.

fields.name: return_reason
fields.description: As given, shown to Accounts.

fields.name: returned_by
fields.description: The acting School Admin.

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.
errors.note: Ask for it; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The acting user is not a School Admin.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. Accounts read it to know what to correct, and often the point is that the instrument is wrong — a credit rather than a cancellation — which only the approver can say.
Never chain a credit onto a return. Where the charge was paid and should be credited, that is Accounts' work in their own session with its own approval (BR-2).
Never return a proposal to defer a decision. A return sends it back for correction with a fault named; where the approver has not decided, it waits.

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. Accounts correct the proposal and raise it again, which is a fresh proposal and a fresh decision.
